additional_info.subject: ID0389470-DC/Si-D/NL-[62D3qS] OCPP Central system reconnect interval CRM:00797001436
additional_info.body:
Dear Thomas,
Thank you for reaching out to eMobility Support. My name is
Sominath
, and I will be assisting you with your following query today:
Product
: Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset
:
MP / S3 170003313
ChargerID/Serial No.
: 62D3qS
Problem Description
: OCPP Central system reconnect interval
Troubleshooting
:
The SICHARGE D charging station is configured with a default OCPP reconnect interval of 30 seconds in the firmware. This is a standard design choice by Siemens to ensure reliable connectivity between the charging station and the OCPP backend system.
If the charging station disconnects from the OCPP backend for any reason, it will automatically attempt to reconnect every 30 seconds until the connection is reestablished.
If the charger is frequently disconnecting from the OCPP backend, it is recommended to configure the OCPP keys as follows: set 'WebSocketPingInterval' to 30 seconds and 'HeartbeatInterval' to 180 seconds. This configuration should be applied on the OCPP backend.
These settings will help maintain the connection between the charging station and the OCPP backend, reducing the need for frequent reconnection attempts.
For future reference, your ticket number is
0389470
, please do refer to this in all further communication regarding this issue.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Sominath Nagalgaon

Hi Thomas,
Thank you for your time and patience.
We accessed the XF4 router via SSH and found that the SIM card status is shown as 'SIM (Not Inserted).'
Was anyone on-site recently for maintenance? It's possible that the door was opened, and when it was closed, the impact caused the SIM card to slip out of place or something.
If that’s not the case, the issue could be hardware-related. In this case, the problem may involve one of the following components:
The SIM card
The SIM card tray
The router itself
We recommend scheduling an on-site visit to inspect these components. Please carry a spare router as a precaution, in case it is needed.

She’ll take over my role for service of the Sicharge D’s.
Since the intervention, the charger hasn’t been online on our platform (that we use for updates and troubleshooting). There are two routers, XF4 is the router for OCPP and XF3 the router for the Siemens platform. I think when checking the OCPP connection someone accidently might have taken out the SIM from XF3 instead of XF4 and not reinserted it properly or e.g. touch the power supply. Would it be possible to have someone check XF3?
Thomas

Hi colleagues,
The customer did, by accident, a factory reset on our router. We reconfigured the router. It's back online now in both OCPP and SCB.
Thomas, ticket can be closed.
